question: According to Table 6B-3, what taper lengths are used for shifting, shoulder, and one-lane two-way traffic tapers?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 6B-3, a shifting taper has a length of at least 0.5 L, a shoulder taper has a length of at least 0.33 L, and a one-lane, two-way traffic taper is 50 feet minimum to 100 feet maximum (L is calculated using Table 6B-4). These are Guidance-level recommendations, not mandatory Standards. Guidance (recommended): - "A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4)." - "If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used." - "A taper having a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with channelizing devices at approximately 20-foot spacing should be used to guide traffic into the one-lane section, and a downstream taper should be used to guide traffic back into their original lane." - "The appropriate taper length (L) should be determined using the criteria shown in Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4." Support (informational): - Tapers are created using a series of channelizing devices and/or pavement markings to move traffic out of or into the normal path; types of tapers are shown in Figure 6B-2. - An example of a one-lane, two-way traffic taper is shown in Figure 6B-3. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 6B-3 listing Shifting Taper "at least 0.5 L," Shoulder Taper "at least 0.33 L," and One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Taper "50 feet minimum, 100 feet maximum," with a note to use Table 6B-4 to calculate L. [Image 2] (Figure 6B-2) depicts shifting tapers dimensioned as 1/2 L and a shoulder taper dimensioned as 1/3 L. [Image 4] shows the full page containing Table 6B-3 with the same taper length criteria alongside Table 6B-4 formulas for calculating L. [Image 3] contains the Guidance text for shifting (½ L), shoulder (⅓ L), and one-lane, two-way tapers (50–100 feet). [Image 5] (Figure 6P-39) illustrates shoulder tapers and 1/2 L shifting taper dimensions in a typical application. Citations: - Table 6B-3 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §8 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §10 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §14 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §4 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Support §2 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Support §15 (p.776) - Page 815 - Page 816 - Page 817 - Page 978
gold_answer: A shifting taper is at least 0.5L, a shoulder taper is at least 0.33L, and a one-lane two-way traffic taper is 50 feet minimum and 100 feet maximum.
